filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Dominican Republic (Olor, Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa)
about: The first General Cigar Cohiba with a Connecticut Shade wrapper, launched in 2019. It is made in the Dominican Republic with a wrapper grown in Ecuador.
notes: This is the non-Cuban Cohiba sold in the US by General Cigar. Retailers split on strength: Famous Smoke says medium, Neptune says mild; the maker rates the body medium. Halfwheel listed the Robusto at 52 ring at launch, the maker now lists 50.
verifyNotes: Removed flavor 'pepper' (not in any source). Rewrote about to drop the maker's 'smoothest' claim. Blend, sizes, factory, 2019 release and the retailer strength split all confirmed.

about: The original non-Cuban Cohiba from General Cigar, nicknamed Red Dot for the red dot inside the O on the band. It pairs a Cameroon wrapper with Dominican filler and is the core line of the US Cohiba brand.
notes: Not the Cuban Cohiba: this is General Cigar's Dominican-made brand, sold only in the US. The maker describes it as full in flavor but medium in strength. A 6 x 60 Gigante has also been offered.

about: A high-priced Cohiba from General Cigar whose filler tobaccos were aged at least four years, finishing in Dominican rum barrels. It is named for the Macassar ebony used on its box.

about: The maduro line in General Cigar's Cohiba range, with a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Dominican and Mexican tobaccos aged at least three years.
notes: Holt's and Neptune list it as medium, Famous Smoke as medium-full; the maker rates the body medium-full.

about: The lower-priced, everyday line in General Cigar's Cohiba range, introduced in 2017. It leans on Honduran tobacco for both wrapper and binder and is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
notes: Retailers list it as medium. The maker's own description calls it medium to full bodied, while its rating scale shows medium. Famous Smoke describes the wrapper and binder as Honduran Olancho San Agustin.
verifyNotes: Removed flavor 'caramel' (not in the listed sources). All other fields confirmed.

about: The first Cohiba from General Cigar to be blended and rolled in Nicaragua, released in 2014. It uses Nicaraguan binder and filler from Estelí and Jalapa under a Colorado Oscuro wrapper.
notes: Not a Nicaraguan puro: halfwheel says the wrapper is Honduran, from Jamastran, and Famous Smoke lists it as Honduran Corojo. Famous and Neptune call it full, Holt's medium-full, and the maker rates the body medium. Sizes have changed since the 2014 launch.

about: Released in 2020 as the fullest-bodied Cohiba from General Cigar and the first one made in Honduras. Its tobaccos are aged five to six years under a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper.
notes: The maker calls it strong and full-bodied and Neptune lists it as full, but Famous Smoke lists medium. Halfwheel's filler list has only Honduras and Nicaragua, while the maker also names Dominican leaf. The 5 1/2 x 54 was first sold under the name Royale.

about: An all-Dominican Cohiba from General Cigar, made only from the company's own Dominican tobaccos aged in tercios and charred wooden barrels. It has been retired from the lineup.
notes: General Cigar's Cigar World site marks this line as retired, and it is no longer on cohiba.com. The maker does not name the wrapper variety beyond Dominican.

about: Launched in 2023 as the only box-pressed line in General Cigar's Cohiba range and the first with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is made in Nicaragua with Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos and no Dominican leaf.
notes: Sources disagree on strength: the maker's launch release said medium to full bodied and cohiba.com now says medium-bodied, while Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as full.

about: The Miami-made line from Cornelius & Anthony, the Bailey family's Virginia cigar company, rolled at El Titan de Bronze. It is named for Cornelius Bailey, who started the family tobacco business in 1866.
notes: The brand appears to be defunct: halfwheel wrote in 2026 that it effectively ended around 2019 after the owners' cigarette company was sold, so any stock is old. The launch announcement listed only Nicaraguan filler; later sources add Dominican.

about: A Brazilian-wrapped blend from Cornelius & Anthony, made at Erik Espinosa's La Zona factory in Estelí. It is a tribute to Mac Bailey, father of company owner Steven Bailey.

about: A full-strength Cornelius & Anthony line made at La Zona in Estelí with Nicaraguan binder and filler under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Its box art shows the patent drawing for the Bailey machine gun.
